title: Spare Key Orchard
theme: giving a neglected orchard another season
lines: The orchard gate has swallowed half my spare brass key
I bring a borrowed ladder and a flask of tea
Your pruning marks are crooked but the branches still agree
An apple splits its paper skin against my knee
Leave one row untended for the birds that stayed
We can count our losses in the afternoon shade

title: Repair Counter
theme: a repair shop closing after decades
lines: A drawer of tiny screws outlives the shop across the street
The radio needs a wire where its two blue rivers meet
You write the final receipt and slide it underneath my hand
A clock without its numbers tells us where we stand
Keep the little bell that rang above the door
It knows a kind of welcome we can still restore

title: Ferry Apron
theme: a cook returning home by ferry
lines: I fold my flour apron as the ferry leaves the pier
A gull steals someone's breakfast while the engines disappear
The island wears a collar made of rain and yellow rope
My pockets hold a pepper seed and half a stubborn hope
Meet me where the road gives up its painted line
There is bread enough for both of us this time

title: Museum Roof
theme: saving ordinary objects from a museum leak
lines: We move the glass display before the ceiling starts to rain
A wedding shoe sits dry beside a map of freight and grain
The guard has found a bucket with a handle made of string
An ordinary teaspoon looks like such a fragile thing
Hold the ladder steady while I lift this box
Someone kept a lifetime in these buttons and these locks

title: Night Nursery
theme: caregiving during a greenhouse night shift
lines: The seedlings lean toward windows that reflect my tired face
I turn the little heaters down and give the roots some space
Your message asks if anything can bloom this late in June
I send a leaf unfolding under one fluorescent moon
Even in the hours when the room forgets the sun
Something small is learning how to carry morning on

title: Chalk Delivery
theme: a delivery worker finishing an unfamiliar route
lines: The chalk address has washed into a pale uncertain cloud
I ask a man with seedlings and he laughs a little loud
His dog escorts my bicycle beyond the broken sign
A woman takes the parcel like the weather has been kind
Every road can borrow a familiar name from you
Every wrong turn leaves me with a different view

title: The Quiet Crane
theme: a crane operator facing retirement
lines: I climb above the harbor with an orange in my coat
The ships below look smaller than the promises we wrote
My replacement brings a thermos and a careful folded chart
I show her how the cables sing before the motors start
Lower down the empty hook and let the morning through
There is room above this city for a newer view

title: Library Seed Box
theme: neighbors sharing seeds at a library
lines: Between the books on weather sits a drawer of borrowed beans
A child has drawn a garden where the catalogue had been
We sign our names in pencil with the dirt still on our hands
Nobody needs to promise what the summer understands
Take a little future in an envelope of brown
Bring a little plenty when the leaves come falling down

title: Floorboard Radio
theme: discovering a message during home repair
lines: The floorboard lifts and offers up a spool of copper wire
A folded station schedule and a photograph of fire
We tune the dusty radio until the voices clear
Somebody kept the smallest sounds that made a home in here
Let the crooked aerial lean against the wall
There is more than empty space beneath the things that fall

title: Raincheck Parade
theme: neighbors improvising a celebration after rain
lines: The cardboard dragon softens in the doorway of the hall
We wring the paper streamers out and hang them on the wall
A drummer taps the windowsill with chopsticks from the tray
The oldest dancer kicks her muddy rubber boots away
Bring the battered lantern where the kettle starts to sing
We can make a festival from almost anything

title: Last Bowling Lane
theme: friends meeting at a closing bowling alley
lines: Lane seven keeps its stubborn lean no matter what we try
Your ball returns like thunder with a sleepy amber eye
We share a plate of oranges beside the rental shoes
The owner lets the jukebox play a song we didn't choose
Leave the score in pencil on the table by the door
I came here for your laughter and I need no more

title: Tin Lunch Star
theme: a parent and child exchanging small keepsakes
lines: You cut a crooked star out of the lid of yesterday
I keep it in my lunchbox while the cranes lift clay
At noon the other workers ask what makes the metal shine
I tell them every sharp little corner has a name like mine
When I bring the empty box back through our door
Put another piece of sky where there was work before

title: Tide Table
theme: a coastal family measuring change
lines: We mark the kitchen doorway with the height the water came
The salt has left a border round the letters of your name
You set the table farther from the window than before
I sweep a tiny beach back underneath the swollen door
Pass the chipped blue pitcher and the bread we saved
We are more than measurements the hungry water made

title: Small Observatory
theme: two friends repairing an amateur telescope
lines: The telescope is balanced on a chair that lost a screw
You clean the cloudy eyepiece with the corner of your blue
A planet shakes like something we could hold inside a spoon
We argue over Saturn then agree to watch the moon
Keep your hand beneath the lens until the shaking ends
The sky is wide enough to let us both begin again

title: Tailor's Window
theme: a tailor adapting a suit for a new life
lines: The tailor chalks a border where my shoulders used to hide
He turns the old coat inside out and sets the fear aside
A pocket keeps a ticket from a town I left in haste
We choose a brighter lining for the years I will not waste
Let the hem fall where my feet can find the floor
I am learning how to stand inside my clothes once more

title: Reservoir Steps
theme: returning to a drained reservoir
lines: The water leaves a staircase that we never knew was there
A bicycle lies sleeping in the cold unborrowed air
You count the missing landings with a stone inside your palm
I hear the old town waiting underneath the sudden calm
We will walk the bank and leave the buried windows closed
Some things need the mercy of a place nobody knows

title: Bakery Shift
theme: a new baker working before dawn
lines: My first tray rises sideways like a row of little sails
The baker says the weather gets a vote in what prevails
I dust the counter slowly while the ovens change their tune
Outside a streetlight flickers like a tired private moon
When the morning finds us let the crooked loaves be seen
There is room upon the table for the places we have been

title: Platform Garden
theme: commuters caring for a station garden
lines: The station keeps a garden in a cracked forgotten cart
We water it with bottles when the evening trains depart
A stranger leaves a label with a name I cannot read
I trust the careful handwriting and give the soil a seed
Something stays beside us while the destinations change
Let the flowers learn our faces from the edge of the rain

title: Painted Oar
theme: siblings restoring a boat after an argument
lines: You sand the painted oar while I repair the narrow seat
Our argument lies drying in the sawdust at our feet
The lake is not a witness and the boat will never ask
We pass the varnish carefully and share the smaller tasks
Push the bow beyond the stones and let the silence bend
We can learn a kinder rhythm before reaching land again

title: Rooftop Laundry
theme: a neighborhood seen from shared laundry lines
lines: The rooftops wear our laundry like a fleet of quiet flags
A pigeon guards the chimney and the wind explores our bags
Your sleeve has found my pillowcase across the narrow lane
We wave without a sentence as the cloth begins to strain
Keep a wooden peg for anything the weather frees
There are ordinary messages that only travel on a breeze

title: Clockmaker's Walk
theme: noticing life after years of precise work
lines: The clockmaker walks slowly with no watch against his skin
He stops beside a puddle where the swallows circle in
A tram arrives a minute late and no one seems to mind
He buys a pear and leaves the paper schedule behind
Let the afternoon arrive without a polished gear
There is time enough to notice who is standing here

title: Frozen Canal
theme: a friendship sustained through winter routines
lines: We carry sacks of birdseed where the canal has turned to glass
Your footprints make a sentence that the drifting snow lets pass
The benches wear white blankets and the boats forget to creak
We talk about the small things we were saving all the week
Bring your oldest mittens and the story I have heard
There is warmth in being known without explaining every word

title: Paper Lantern Shift
theme: a hospital worker heading home after a festival
lines: The festival is over when I leave the ward at dawn
One lantern floats above the bins with half its paper gone
My shoes remember corridors my mouth cannot describe
The tea stall keeps a burner for the workers passing by
Set a little cup beside the steam and let it stay
I need a gentler threshold on the other side of day

title: Empty Aquarium
theme: starting over in a newly rented apartment
lines: The last tenant left an empty tank beneath the kitchen light
I fill it up with seedlings instead of fish tonight
A plastic castle shelters all the cuttings you brought round
Our borrowed little kingdom has its roots above the ground
Let the window gather every shade of green it can
We can start with what is here and make a softer plan

title: Accordion Case
theme: a musician finding a different use for an old case
lines: The accordion is gone but its case still smells of rain
I carry tools inside it on the crowded morning train
A child asks for a melody and I offer her a screw
She calls it silver music and her mother smiles too
Every shape can hold another kind of useful sound
Keep the worn old handle till a new song comes around

title: Market Umbrella
theme: market sellers helping a newcomer
lines: My market umbrella opens with a noise like startled geese
The fruit seller beside me brings a brick to keep the peace
She teaches me the knots that hold against the river air
I trade a jar of marmalade for all her patient care
When the canvas starts to pull we can lean against the same
There is shelter in a neighbor who has learned your name

title: Underpass Choir
theme: strangers briefly singing together under a bridge
lines: The underpass gives every footstep twice the room it needs
A busker hums a note that splits the traffic into beads
We wait beneath the dripping arch until the shower thins
Somebody adds a harmony and everybody grins
Let the tunnel keep a little echo when we go
We were briefly more than strangers with our collars full of snow

title: Unsent Postcards
theme: choosing to reconnect through a small message
lines: The postcards in the cupboard show a coast I never knew
I bought them for the colors when I meant to write to you
Today I choose the lighthouse with the crooked crimson beam
And tell you how the kettle broke instead of how I dream
There is room beneath the picture for a plain and honest start
Even ordinary weather makes a doorway to the heart

title: Mending Sail
theme: a sailing club repairing equipment together
lines: We spread the torn sail over every table in the room
The youngest sailor threads a needle under pale afternoon
Our patches make an atlas of the jackets we outgrew
The harbor bell keeps asking when the work will carry through
Stitch the stubborn corners where the heavy weather bit
There is strength inside the places we decided not to quit

title: Orange Peel Map
theme: a long bus ride interrupted by kindness
lines: An orange peel uncoils across the map upon my knee
The driver stops for someone only half the rest can see
A suitcase full of seedlings takes the vacant aisle seat
We share the fruit and watch the mountains soften in the heat
Mark the little layby where the journey learned to bend
We can lose a minute and arrive with one more friend

title: The Spare Chair
theme: preparing a community meal for an unknown guest
lines: We set another chair beside the patched green folding table
The cook says leave it open for whoever might be able
A pot of beans keeps talking while the doorway fills with steam
I fold a paper napkin into something like a dream
You can come with empty pockets and a story left untold
There is always one more place before the supper turns cold

title: Glasshouse Hail
theme: neighbors repairing storm damage
lines: The hail has left a thousand little windows in the roof
We drape the glasshouse carefully in sheets of borrowed blue
Your seedlings stand like question marks against the battered trays
I write their names on wooden sticks and promise warmer days
Bring the tape and bring the stool and bring your stubborn hands
We can make a little shelter where the broken garden stands

title: Ceramic Bird
theme: keeping an imperfect handmade gift
lines: The ceramic bird has one wing thicker than the other
You wrapped it in a tea towel that once belonged to mother
It balances beside the sink and watches dishes shine
I turn its face toward morning when the first sun crosses mine
Let the careful little cracks collect a little gold
Some gifts grow more familiar every time we let them hold

title: Bookmobile Hill
theme: a traveling librarian reaching an isolated village
lines: The bookmobile climbs slowly with its cupboards tied in place
A jar of loose bookmarks rattles near the driver's face
At the hilltop children gather in a ring of muddy shoes
Each spine becomes a doorway they can open as they choose
Park beside the chestnut where the road forgets its name
Bring a world of other weather when the valley feels the same

title: Wind Farm Lunch
theme: finding stillness beneath large machines
lines: The turbines turn above us while we unwrap bread and cheese
Their shadows cross the thermos like a slow enormous breeze
You point toward a kestrel keeping pace against the blade
We leave a little silence in the shelter we have made
Let the engines have the distance let the grass receive our weight
We can sit beside the motion without learning how to race

title: The Lost Glove Rack
theme: small acts of care in a public park
lines: The keeper nails a board beside the gate for missing gloves
A tiny purple mitten waits among the larger loves
You recognize the striped one that the winter took from me
I leave a clip behind for anything we cannot see
Hang the little losses where a passing hand can reach
There are ways of saying welcome that nobody needs to teach

title: Quarry Echo
theme: friends revisiting a quarry as it becomes a park
lines: The quarry has a footpath where the yellow trucks once stood
We follow painted arrows through a narrow strip of wood
Your father cut the limestone that the new park benches wear
You touch the rough underside and find his working there
Let the water gather slowly where the drills once shook the ground
There are other kinds of living in the echo of that sound

title: Snowplow Flowers
theme: spring arriving at a municipal depot
lines: The snowplow rests beside a crate of early daffodils
A mechanic oils the hinges while the rain descends the hills
You plant a row of yellow where the salt bags used to lie
I write a label for the flowers that the trucks keep passing by
Let the heavy winter tools grow quiet in their shed
Something bright can find a home where all that cold was led

title: Borrowed Projector
theme: showing homemade films in a village hall
lines: We borrow a projector with a handle wrapped in tape
A bedsheet takes the evening in a crooked silver shape
The children laugh at shadows while we try to thread the reel
Your grandfather's small garden makes the whole room suddenly still
Keep a little empty wall for memories to move
There is more than one kind of light a village can improve

title: Pocket Compass
theme: learning a familiar walk after a life change
lines: The pocket compass points across the kitchen toward the park
I take it on our usual walk though every path is marked
The bakery has a new blue door the old dog isn't there
I stop to tie a shoelace and make room for different air
Let the needle find its north while I find something near
There is more than one direction for a life to open here
